text.en: The best way to predict the future is to invent it.
text.zh: 预测未来的最好方法就是创造它。

commentary.en: Not forecasting. Not waiting for permission. Build the future you actually want to live in — and think in decades, not quarters.
commentary.zh: 不是预测，也不是等许可。去建造你想活在其中的未来——以十年为单位思考，而不是以季度。

text.en: Everything should be made as simple as possible, but not simpler.
text.zh: 凡事都应尽可能简单，但不能更简单。

commentary.en: Simplification has a floor. The goal is not fewer lines of code — it is less cognitive load, without sanding off the part that was actually hard.
commentary.zh: 简化是有底线的。目标不是更少的代码行数，而是更小的心智负担——还不能把真正难的那一层磨掉。

text.en: The most dangerous thought you can have as a creative person is to think you know what you're doing.
text.zh: 作为创意工作者，你能有的最危险的想法就是认为自己知道自己在做什么。

commentary.en: Stay a beginner. Expertise calcifies into a prison — the best ideas still come from naive questions.
commentary.zh: 保持初学者心态。专业知识会慢慢变成牢笼——最好的想法，往往还是来自天真的问题。

commentary.en: Parenthesize it two ways and both are true: don't chase popularity if it costs the idea; and sometimes staying small is how the idea stays free. I wrote a whole note about this after watching SPJ's Haskell journey talk.
commentary.zh: 两种括法都成立：不要为了流行而牺牲想法本身；有时保持小众，想法才能自由。看完 SPJ 讲 Haskell 的那通分享，我专门写过一篇笔记。

quotes.author: Cheng Lou
quotes.source: Reason / React, via 「程序员中的梦想家」

commentary.en: The tools look messy while they are being invented. Visionaries get underestimated on the way up and mythologized after. If you are in the pit with them — that's the job.
commentary.zh: 东西在被发明的时候看起来都很糟。梦想家在过程中被低估，流行之后又被神化。如果你正在坑里跟他们一起填——那就是这份工作。

commentary.en: "Pressure is a privilege, and champions adjust." If you feel the weight, you already earned a moment that matters. Reframe it as proof you belong on the floor.
commentary.zh: "压力是一种荣幸，而冠军懂得调整。" 你能感到这份重量，说明你已经凭实力站上了这个场合。把它重新理解为：你有资格在场。

statement.en: Frameworks should be discovered, not invented.
statement.zh: 框架应该被发现，而非发明。

en: Years of watching invented abstractions fail
React emerging from Facebook's actual product needs
zh: 多年来目睹发明出来的抽象层失败
React 从 Facebook 真实产品需求里长出来

reasoning.en: Good frameworks show up after you have solved the same real problem enough times. Invented frameworks solve imaginary problems — very elegantly.
reasoning.zh: 好的框架来自反复解决同一个真问题。发明的框架，则优雅地解决想象中的问题。

statement.zh: 演示驱动，而非规格驱动。

en: Dan Abramov
Lynx team culture
zh: Dan Abramov
Lynx 团队文化

reasoning.en: A spec describes what you think you want. A demo reveals what you actually need. Show me, don't tell me.
reasoning.zh: 规格写的是你以为你想要的。演示揭开的是你真正需要的。给我看，别只告诉我。

statement.en: Absorb complexity into the compiler. Fast by default.
statement.zh: 把复杂度吸收进编译器。默认就该很快。

en: React Forget / React Compiler
Hermes
Lynx's dual-thread runtime
zh: React Forget / React Compiler
Hermes
Lynx 的双线程运行时

reasoning.en: The worst tax in UI programming is asking every product engineer to be a performance expert. If the authoring model is clean, the compiler and the runtime should do the remembering — memo, threads, dependencies — so the default path is already the fast path.
reasoning.zh: UI 编程最重的税，是要求每个业务工程师都先成为性能专家。如果编写模型本身是干净的，记忆化、线程、依赖这些事就该由编译器和运行时来做——让默认路径就是快路径。

en: Thinking in React vs. Thinking in Vue
Hooks' referential-identity tax
zh: Thinking in React vs. Thinking in Vue
Hooks 的引用同一性税

reasoning.en: Two systems can expose the same features and still be incomparable, because they ask you to think differently. Copy the API and you have copied nothing. The hard part is the model — and the consistency it demands.
reasoning.zh: 两套系统可以功能对等，却完全无法类比，因为它们要求你用不同的方式思考。抄了 API，等于什么都没抄到。难的是模型，以及模型所要求的一致性。

statement.en: Stay a tourist at the glowing edge of what you don't understand.
statement.zh: 在「看不懂集」发光的边缘，继续当游客。

en: Matt Might's illustrated guide to a Ph.D.
The jump from frontend into PL / compilers
zh: Matt Might 的「博士是什么」
从前端跳进编程语言与编译器

reasoning.en: For any field I actually know, I can name a pile of things I don't. That set grows faster than what I learn. The work is not to finish knowing — it is to pick, from an ever-larger unread set, the next subset still worth touring.
reasoning.zh: 对任何一个我真正了解的领域，我都能列出一大堆看不懂的东西。那个集合比我学会的东西涨得更快。要做的不是把知识学完，而是在愈发巨大的「看不懂集」里，挑出下一片还愿意去逛的子集。

statement.en: Build tools for thought, not tools for output.
statement.zh: 构建思考的工具，而非产出的工具。

en: Bret Victor
Doug Engelbart
zh: Bret Victor
Doug Engelbart

reasoning.en: The best tools don't just emit artifacts. They change how you think about the problem space.
reasoning.zh: 最好的工具不只是吐产物——它们会改变你思考问题空间的方式。

statement.en: You are always becoming. Narrative is how you answer who you are.
statement.zh: 人永远都在 Becoming。叙事就是在回答「你是谁」。

en: Personal storytelling across three year career cycles
zh: 以三年为周期的个人叙事

reasoning.en: Identity is not a title you freeze. Each era, consumer, producer, architect, is a rewrite, not a reveal.
reasoning.zh: 身份不是冻结的头衔。每个时代，消费者、生产者、架构师，都是一次重写，而不是揭晓。

en: Demo-driven, not spec-driven
Explains from the user's side of the API
Makes the complex simple — without making it simpler
zh: 演示驱动，而非规格驱动
从 API 使用者的一侧开始解释
让复杂变简单，但不更简单

en: Relentless pursuit of better interfaces
Demos that change how you see the world
Unwilling to accept the status quo
zh: 不懈追求更好的界面
能改变你看世界方式的演示
不愿接受现状

en: Invented the future he wanted to see
Thinking in decades, not quarters
Objects were about messaging, not data
zh: 发明了他想看到的未来
以十年为单位思考，而非季度
对象是关于消息传递，而非数据

en: The hacker and the painter are the same kind of maker
Taste is a technical skill
Essays that made it legitimate to care about both code and art
zh: 黑客与画家是同一种创造者
品味本身是一种技术能力
让「既写代码又在乎艺术」变成一件正经事

en: The web as a distribution and power question, not a framework question
Uncomfortable honesty about what browsers actually afford
Still the clearest writer I know on platform economics
zh: 把 Web 当成分发与权力的问题，而不是框架的问题
对浏览器真正能提供什么，诚实得让人不舒服
讲平台经济学，仍是我读过最清楚的人之一
